# Fixed semantic registration plan

The offline adapter builder uses the existing Trimesh5.1.1 implementation of Sumner/Popovic deformation-transfer registration, with Amberg as a bounded comparison. Primary implementation documentation: https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh/blob/main/docs/content/nricp.md and https://trimesh.org/trimesh.registration.html . The correspondence stage and runtime deformation transfer are separate; a small closest-surface residual alone does not certify semantic correctness.

Actual restored components: GNM has17821 vertices and six labelled components (skin12466, each eye771, upper/lower teeth and gums1440 each, tongue933). Its skin's20 named facial regions cover4592 vertices; the rest has region255. Anny has13718 vertices and four connected components, including two72-vertex eye components. MHR has18439 vertices in one connected component, so connected-component separation alone cannot identify its eyes/lips/mouth.

Next evidence: render neutral teacher geometry under one documented frontal camera convention; use the already published MediaPipe/Google GNM473-correspondence table only to propose semantic constraints. GNM source points must be actual native template vertices, never the table's calibrated reference point cloud. Raycast every accepted target landmark onto actual teacher triangles and record its camera, face and barycentrics. Inspect eye/lip constraints before solving. Register exterior skin with semantic masks and keep eye and mouth interior components separate. Verify upper/lower lip order, eyelid/eyeball correspondence, triangle orientation, material-region coverage, and paired age/expression renders before enabling transferred controls.

The neutral registration can be calculated offline, but any runtime transfer must remain lightweight and preserve the same vertex/index arrays. Store the exact source hashes, generator version and compact mapping in Git at each accepted checkpoint. Imported teacher data is reused by URL/hash and is not rebundled.

The initial all-skin registration exposed an important mismatch: its worst26mm/54mm nearest-surface residuals were the GNM oral back wall, not outer facial mismatch. Removing the native upper/lower-lip semantic boundary from the graph isolates464 oral-skin vertices; removing the nose boundary isolates two76-vertex nasal cavities. These are preserved separately. Exterior registration therefore uses11850 native skin vertices, with the boundary regions reinserted. Both smooth and official-default solver presets are retained, with their original residual reports; none is yet a semantic-quality pass.
